title: CVE-2022-27781: CERTINFO never-ending busy-loop
explain: The real code shows the flaw the report describes.

problems.evidence: lib/vtls/nss.c existed in curl's history but not at bc677a8f16a5

summary: Curl is prone to a DoS attack in case the NSS TLS library is used and the CERTINFO option is enabled. Using maliciously crafted certificates on a server, an attacker can make curl run into an endless loop when connecting to the server.

claims.text: display_conn_info() runs into an endless loop when the received certificate chain contains a loop
claims.reasoning: The while loop at lines 1019-1028 traverses the issuer chain using CERT_FindCertIssuer but maintains no visited-certificate set. If the chain contains a cycle (e.g., CA1 issued by CA2, CA2 issued by CA1), cert2 never becomes NULL and cert2->isRoot is never true, so the loop never terminates.

citations.note: while(cert2) loop with no cycle detection; if certificate chain has a loop, cert2 never becomes NULL and cert2->isRoot never true
only exit condition is cert2->isRoot, which is never true in a mutual-issuer loop
cert3 = CERT_FindCertIssuer(cert2, ...) continues the chain traversal
cert2 = cert3 advances to next issuer without visited-set tracking

claims.text: display_conn_info() starts with the leaf certificate and attempts to find its issuer certificate in the chain
claims.reasoning: The function starts with the peer (leaf) certificate at line 1005 and immediately attempts to find its issuer at line 1018.

citations.note: cert = SSL_PeerCertificate(sock) obtains the leaf certificate
cert2 = CERT_FindCertIssuer(cert, now, certUsageSSLCA) finds the leaf's issuer

claims.reasoning: The loop condition at line 1019 and the repeated issuer lookup at line 1025 will follow a cyclic chain indefinitely because there is no cycle detection.

citations.note: while(cert2) continues as long as an issuer is found
CERT_FindCertIssuer called repeatedly on each successive certificate

claims.text: application runs into an infinite loop and consumes nearly 100% CPU
claims.reasoning: An infinite loop with no blocking calls (only CERT_FindCertIssuer and CERT_DestroyCertificate) will consume 100% CPU.

citations.note: i++ executes on every iteration with no bound

claims.text: modify URL in certinfo example to point to https://localhost:4443/ and execute certinfo
claims.reasoning: The example enables CERTINFO and sets a URL; changing the URL to the malicious server reproduces the issue.

citations.note: curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_URL, "https://www.example.com/"); -- the line to modify

claims.text: build curl with NSS TLS library and with examples
claims.reasoning: The vulnerable code is in the NSS-specific TLS backend (lib/vtls/nss.c), so building with --with-nss is required.

citations.note: display_conn_info is compiled only when NSS backend is used

key_reasons: The while loop at lib/vtls/nss.c:1019-1028 traverses the certificate issuer chain without any cycle detection.
If a server presents a certificate chain with a loop (mutual issuers), CERT_FindCertIssuer will keep returning certificates indefinitely.
The only loop exit conditions are cert2 becoming NULL or cert2->isRoot being true; neither occurs in a cyclic chain.
The vulnerability is reachable when CERTINFO is enabled (line 1009) and the NSS backend is used.
An attacker controlling a TLS server can trigger this DoS against any libcurl application built with NSS and CERTINFO enabled.
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and PoC. The infinite loop in display_conn_info() when processing a cyclic certificate chain is confirmed in lib/vtls/nss.c lines 1019-1028. The while loop lacks cycle detection, so a malicious server presenting mutually-issued CA certificates causes a DoS. We will add a visited-certificate check to bound the traversal.
